tasks.instruction: Return true when both values have the same top 8 bits (bits 24 to 31) and the first value's lowest byte is not zero.
tasks.note: Second shift amount wrong; the wrong edit shifts by 23 and so also compares bit 23.

tasks.instruction: Return the sum of three consecutive elements starting at the given index, where positions past the end wrap around to the start.
tasks.note: Third element offset wrong (3 instead of 2); wrong edit repeats the second element.

tasks.instruction: Given scores p0, p1 and entrant numbers p2, p3, return true when the first entrant wins: a higher score wins, and on equal scores the strictly lower entrant number wins.
tasks.note: Equal entrant numbers must not win; wrong edit lets every score tie win.

tasks.instruction: Pack the low bytes of the four arguments into one word: the first argument in bits 0 to 7, the second in bits 8 to 15, the third in bits 16 to 23 and the fourth in bits 24 to 31.
tasks.note: Third byte shifted into the second byte's place; wrong edit drops the mask on the third argument.

tasks.instruction: The function returns 10 per cent of the amount rounded down; change it to return 15 per cent rounded down, exact for every amount without overflow.
tasks.note: Both rate constants must change; a direct multiply-then-divide wraps for large amounts.

tasks.instruction: f folds step over the array to find the position of the largest element. Change step so that when an element equals the best so far, the earlier position is kept.
tasks.note: Ties must not replace the stored position; one wrong edit inverts the test, the other compares with the stored position.

tasks.instruction: Read the low 16 bits as a two's-complement signed number and return its magnitude and whether it is negative; bit 15 set means negative.
tasks.note: Boundary at 32768 (the most negative value) must count as negative; wrong edit is off by one in the magnitude.

tasks.instruction: Write the value into the given position and also into the mirrored position counted from the other end (position 0 mirrors 3, 1 mirrors 2), positions taken modulo 4.
tasks.note: Mirror index is 3 minus the position; wrong edit subtracts the other way.

tasks.instruction: Shift the value right by the distance as now, but also set bit 0 of the result whenever any 1 bit was shifted out.
tasks.note: Sticky bit set when shifting back does not restore the value; wrong edits invert the test or test the result instead.

tasks.instruction: Using the helper, which gives the larger of a value's two 16-bit halves, return true when the first value's larger half is strictly greater than the second value's.
tasks.note: Second call must use the second argument; wrong edit swaps the comparison.

tasks.instruction: f returns true when every element of the array is strictly below the limit. Fix the per-element check, which currently accepts an element equal to the limit.
tasks.note: Strict bound; wrong edit reverses the comparison.

tasks.instruction: Convert a Celsius temperature to Fahrenheit: multiply by 9, divide by 5 rounding down, then add 32.
tasks.note: Two constants swapped and the offset wrong; dividing first loses the remainder.

tasks.instruction: Versions are packed as major in the top 16 bits and minor in the low 16. Return true when the installed version (first) has the same major as the required one (second) and a minor at least as high.
tasks.note: Equal minor must be accepted; wrong edits mask too few bits or accept a newer major.

tasks.instruction: Return true when the current time (first) has reached the alarm time (second) plus the snooze delay (third); the sum may exceed the u32 range, so do not add them.
tasks.note: Adding alarm and delay wraps to a small value; the wrong edit forgets that the current time may be before the alarm.

tasks.instruction: Return the array with each neighbouring pair exchanged: elements 0 and 1 trade places, and elements 2 and 3 trade places.
tasks.note: Only the first pair was swapped; wrong edit reverses the whole array.

tasks.instruction: Return how many consecutive 1 bits the value has starting from bit 0 (for example 0b0111 gives 3 and all ones gives 32).
tasks.note: All 32 bits must be examined; 33 steps wraps the shift and rereads bit 0.
